1: import type { CardRow } from '../types';
2: import type { OwnedCard } from './synergy';
3: 
4: /**
5:  * Commander is a singleton format (rule 903.5b): apart from basic lands, a
6:  * deck may not contain more than one card with a given English name.
7:  *
8:  * That matters for recommendations, not just deck legality. A list pasted
9:  * from a collection or a draft pool can carry ten copies of a common, and
10:  * counting all ten would let one card impersonate a whole strategy ΓÇö ten
11:  * Rats reading as a Rats deck you could not actually build.
12:  */
13: 
14: // The two ways a card grants its own exemption. Both are printed rules text,
15: // so they are read off the card rather than kept as a hardcoded name list
16: // that would go stale every set.
17: const ANY_NUMBER = /a deck can have any number of cards named/i;
18: const UP_TO_N = /a deck can have up to (\w+) cards named/i;
19: 
20: // Only ever needed for the handful of "up to N" cards that exist (Seven
21: // Dwarves, Nazg├╗l), but spelled out generously so a new one does not
22: // silently fall back to 1.
23: const NUMBER_WORDS: Record<string, number> = {
24:   one: 1,
25:   two: 2,
26:   three: 3,
27:   four: 4,
28:   five: 5,
29:   six: 6,
30:   seven: 7,
31:   eight: 8,
32:   nine: 9,
33:   ten: 10,
34:   eleven: 11,
35:   twelve: 12,
36: };
37: 
38: /**
39:  * How many copies of this card a Commander deck may legally contain.
40:  * `Infinity` for basic lands and the "any number" cards.
41:  */
42: export function singletonLimit(row: CardRow): number {
43:   // Exempt by supertype rather than by name, which covers snow basics
44:   // ("Basic Snow Land ΓÇö Forest") and Wastes without enumerating anything.
45:   // Both halves are required: "Land ΓÇö Forest" is a nonbasic Forest.
46:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';
47:   if (/\bBasic\b/i.test(typeLine) && /\bLand\b/i.test(typeLine)) return Infinity;
48: 
49:   const text = row.oracle_text ?? '';
50:   if (ANY_NUMBER.test(text)) return Infinity;
51: 
52:   const capped = UP_TO_N.exec(text);
53:   if (capped) {
54:     // Group 1 is mandatory in UP_TO_N, so a match always populates it.
55:     const limit = NUMBER_WORDS[capped[1]!.toLowerCase()];
56:     if (limit) return limit;
57:   }
58: 
59:   return 1;
60: }
61: 
62: export interface SingletonResult {
63:   owned: OwnedCard[];
64:   /** Copies dropped for exceeding the format's limit, so the user can be told. */
65:   ignoredCopies: number;
66: }
67: 
68: /**
69:  * Collapses a parsed list to what could legally be in one Commander deck.
70:  *
71:  * Also merges repeats of the same card, which the list parser deliberately
72:  * does not do ΓÇö a card can appear on several lines ("1 Sol Ring" twice, or
73:  * once in the deck and once in a sideboard section) rather than as a single
74:  * line with a count. Without merging, those would survive as separate
75:  * entries and each be counted as a distinct card supporting a theme.
76:  */
77: export function applySingletonLimits(owned: OwnedCard[]): SingletonResult {
78:   const byCard = new Map<string, OwnedCard>();
79:   for (const entry of owned) {
80:     const existing = byCard.get(entry.row.oracle_id);
81:     // A fresh object rather than mutating the caller's entry ΓÇö the raw list
82:     // is still needed to report how many copies were submitted.
83:     if (existing) existing.quantity += entry.quantity;
84:     else byCard.set(entry.row.oracle_id, { row: entry.row, quantity: entry.quantity });
85:   }
86: 
87:   let ignoredCopies = 0;
88:   const result: OwnedCard[] = [];
89:   for (const entry of byCard.values()) {
90:     const allowed = Math.min(entry.quantity, singletonLimit(entry.row));
91:     ignoredCopies += entry.quantity - allowed;
92:     result.push({ row: entry.row, quantity: allowed });
93:   }
94: 
95:   return { owned: result, ignoredCopies };
96: }

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions ΓÇö
including Partner/Background pairs ΓÇö with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time ΓÇö the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first ΓÇö it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root ΓÇö API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` ΓÇö downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded ΓÇö see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /
  `pnpm test` (Vitest, 5 files colocated under `src/lib/`)
- `pnpm run lint` in either ΓÇö no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score ΓÇö see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander ΓÇö see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card
  or a legal pair) from the eligible pool ΓÇö a `CommanderUnit` is what `synergy.ts` scores, not a
  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, PartnerΓÇö[text], Partner with [Name], Friends
  forever, Choose a Background, Doctor's companion) rather than a cross-product.
- **`server/src/services/eligibility.ts`** judges commander eligibility on a card's **front face
  only** (CR 712.4) ΓÇö Scryfall's top-level `type_line` for a DFC is both faces joined, which is why
  this can't just substring-match the whole thing. `split` is the deliberate exception (CR 709.4).
  This runs at import time (`import-scryfall.ts`'s only caller), so a stale `cards.sqlite` keeps
  old eligibility until re-imported.
- **`server/src/db.ts`** ΓÇö SQLite connection + `isSeeded` guard (returns 503 instead of a raw SQL
  error pre-import) + `findCardsByNames`, which falls back to a `card_face_names` table (built by
  `cardNames.ts`'s rules) so a decklist naming only one face of a DFC still resolves.
- **`server/scripts/fetch-scryfall.ts`** + **`import-scryfall.ts`** are the only place Scryfall is
  called from this app ΓÇö see [`../../docs/api-policy.md`](../../docs/api-policy.md), a hard
  project rule, before changing what these call or when.
- **`server/src/services/spellbook.ts`** ΓÇö Commander Spellbook adapter. Click-triggered only, 1-hour
  in-memory cache, no retry on 429. Same hard-rule constraints apply.
- **Cited-card dedup**: the server sends each cited card once (`server/src/services/cardIndex.ts`)
  and cites it by position; `client/src/lib/rehydrate.ts` puts cards back together at the API
  boundary. This is why a 12MB response became 0.25MB (see `CHANGELOG.md` 1.7.1) ΓÇö don't bypass it
  by threading whole card objects through a new code path.
- **`client/src/api/`** ΓÇö `client.ts` (fetch + cold-start retry against Render's free-tier sleep)
  wrapped by `queries.ts` (TanStack Query hooks). The `retry`/`refetchOnWindowFocus`/
  `refetchOnReconnect: false` defaults in `main.tsx` are load-bearing against Commander
  Spellbook traffic ΓÇö don't restore them without re-reading the api-policy doc.
- **`client/src/store/`** splits by what the state _is_: `useAppStore` (not persisted ΓÇö textarea
  contents, submitted list, dismissals) vs. `usePreferencesStore` (persisted to `localStorage` ΓÇö
  durable UI prefs like page size). Don't merge these; a dismissal surviving a browser restart
  against a different pasted list would be surprising, but a page-size choice should outlive the
  tab.
- **`client/src/lib/mtg.ts`** ΓÇö WUBRG ordering and color-identity naming ("Golgari", never
  "Black/Green"). **`client/src/lib/manaSymbols.ts`** ΓÇö inlined SVG mana glyph paths (see
  `docs/rules-audit.md` item 16 ΓÇö this file is a Phase 2 migration target for `@mtg/mana`).
- A suggestion is a `CommanderUnit` (1-2 `CardRow`s), not a single card ΓÇö every DTO, filter, and
  sort in the client threads through that union, not a flattened card.

## Conventions

- Comments explain _why_, not _what_ ΓÇö match the existing tone (see `synergy.ts`'s comments on the
  scoring formula, or `eligibility.ts`'s on front-face-only reasoning).
- Keep changes proportional to the ask. This codebase deliberately favors a short, readable
  heuristic over a "complete" system in synergy detection and Bracket estimation ΓÇö see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.
- **Never write oracle text from memory ΓÇö copy it from the database.** Scryfall has moved much
  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this
  codebase were written from recall and were wrong on real cards (see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Known risk areas"). Every string in `signals.test.ts` is
  copied verbatim from the imported database ΓÇö keep it that way.
- Before opening a PR: typecheck and test both `client/` and `server/`, and actually run the app
  for anything user-visible ΓÇö a clean typecheck and passing tests are necessary, not sufficient
  (they don't catch a CSS rule that silently stopped applying, for instance).
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` for any user-facing change, in the existing
  style (see `1.7.1`'s entry for the level of detail expected).
- `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map is meant to stay current ΓÇö update it in the same
  commit whenever you add, rename, or remove a file it lists.

1: /**
2:  * Tests for Commander's singleton rule (903.5b) as applied to a submitted
3:  * list.
4:  */
5: import assert from 'node:assert';
6: import { describe, it } from 'vitest';
7: import type { CardRow } from '../types';
8: import { applySingletonLimits, singletonLimit } from './singleton';
9: import type { OwnedCard } from './synergy';
10: 
11: let counter = 0;
12: function makeCard(overrides: Partial<CardRow> = {}): CardRow {
13:   const name = overrides.name ?? `Test Card ${counter++}`;
14:   return {
15:     oracle_id: overrides.oracle_id ?? name,
16:     name,
17:     name_lower: name.toLowerCase(),
18:     mana_cost: null,
19:     cmc: 0,
20:     type_line: 'Creature ΓÇö Human',
21:     oracle_text: '',
22:     colors: '[]',
23:     color_identity: '[]',
24:     keywords: '[]',
25:     creature_types: '[]',
26:     power: '1',
27:     toughness: '1',
28:     scryfall_uri: null,
29:     partner_ability: null,
30:     partner_target: null,
31:     is_background: 0,
32:     legality_commander: 'legal',
33:     game_changer: 0,
34:     is_legendary: 0,
35:     is_commander_eligible: 0,
36:     image_uri: null,
37:     back_image_uri: null,
38:     back_name: null,
39:     ...overrides,
40:   };
41: }
42: 
43: function owned(row: CardRow, quantity = 1): OwnedCard {
44:   return { row, quantity };
45: }
46: 
47: describe('singletonLimit', () => {
48:   it('an ordinary card is limited to a single copy', () => {
49:     assert.strictEqual(singletonLimit(makeCard({ name: 'Sol Ring', type_line: 'Artifact' })), 1);
50:   });
51: 
52:   it('basic lands are unlimited', () => {
53:     assert.strictEqual(
54:       singletonLimit(makeCard({ name: 'Swamp', type_line: 'Basic Land ΓÇö Swamp' })),
55:       Infinity,
56:     );
57:   });
58: 
59:   it('snow basics and Wastes are unlimited too', () => {
60:     // Exempted by supertype, so neither needs naming individually.
61:     assert.strictEqual(
62:       singletonLimit(
63:         makeCard({ name: 'Snow-Covered Forest', type_line: 'Basic Snow Land ΓÇö Forest' }),
64:       ),
65:       Infinity,
66:     );
67:     assert.strictEqual(
68:       singletonLimit(makeCard({ name: 'Wastes', type_line: 'Basic Land' })),
69:       Infinity,
70:     );
71:   });
72: 
73:   it('a nonbasic land sharing a basic land type is still singleton', () => {
74:     // "Land ΓÇö Forest" (e.g. a dual) is not a *basic* Forest.
75:     assert.strictEqual(
76:       singletonLimit(makeCard({ name: 'Bayou', type_line: 'Land ΓÇö Swamp Forest' })),
77:       1,
78:     );
79:   });
80: 
81:   it('"any number" cards are unlimited', () => {
82:     const rats = makeCard({
83:       name: 'Relentless Rats',
84:       oracle_text: 'A deck can have any number of cards named Relentless Rats.',
85:     });
86:     assert.strictEqual(singletonLimit(rats), Infinity);
87:   });
88: 
89:   it('"up to N" cards are limited to N', () => {
90:     const dwarves = makeCard({
91:       name: 'Seven Dwarves',
92:       oracle_text: 'A deck can have up to seven cards named Seven Dwarves.',
93:     });
94:     assert.strictEqual(singletonLimit(dwarves), 7);
95:     const nazgul = makeCard({
96:       name: 'Nazg├╗l',
97:       oracle_text: 'A deck can have up to nine cards named Nazg├╗l.',
98:     });
99:     assert.strictEqual(singletonLimit(nazgul), 9);
100:   });
101: });
102: 
103: describe('applySingletonLimits', () => {
104:   it('extra copies of an ordinary card are dropped', () => {
105:     const solRing = makeCard({ name: 'Sol Ring', type_line: 'Artifact' });
106:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(solRing, 4)]);
107:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned.length, 1);
108:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned[0]!.quantity, 1);
109:     assert.strictEqual(result.ignoredCopies, 3);
110:   });
111: 
112:   it('basic lands keep every copy', () => {
113:     const swamp = makeCard({ name: 'Swamp', type_line: 'Basic Land ΓÇö Swamp' });
114:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(swamp, 12)]);
115:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned[0]!.quantity, 12);
116:     assert.strictEqual(result.ignoredCopies, 0);
117:   });
118: 
119:   it('an "up to N" card keeps N copies and drops the rest', () => {
120:     const dwarves = makeCard({
121:       name: 'Seven Dwarves',
122:       oracle_text: 'A deck can have up to seven cards named Seven Dwarves.',
123:     });
124:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(dwarves, 10)]);
125:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned[0]!.quantity, 7);
126:     assert.strictEqual(result.ignoredCopies, 3);
127:   });
128: 
129:   it('the same card on several lines is merged, then limited', () => {
130:     // The list parser does not combine repeated lines, so this is the shape a
131:     // real paste produces when a card appears in two sections.
132:     const solRing = makeCard({ name: 'Sol Ring', type_line: 'Artifact' });
133:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(solRing, 1), owned(solRing, 1), owned(solRing, 1)]);
134:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned.length, 1);
135:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned[0]!.quantity, 1);
136:     assert.strictEqual(result.ignoredCopies, 2);
137:   });
138: 
139:   it('merging repeats does not let one card pose as several distinct cards', () => {
140:     // The signal threshold counts distinct cards, so three lines of one card
141:     // must collapse to one entry rather than reading as three supporters.
142:     const seer = makeCard({ name: 'Viscera Seer', oracle_text: 'Sacrifice a creature: scry 1.' });
143:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(seer), owned(seer), owned(seer)]);
144:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned.length, 1);
145:   });
146: 
147:   it('distinct cards are all kept', () => {
148:     const a = makeCard({ name: 'Card A' });
149:     const b = makeCard({ name: 'Card B' });
150:     const result = applySingletonLimits([owned(a), owned(b)]);
151:     assert.strictEqual(result.owned.length, 2);
152:     assert.strictEqual(result.ignoredCopies, 0);
153:   });
154: 
155:   it("the caller's entries are not mutated", () => {
156:     const solRing = makeCard({ name: 'Sol Ring', type_line: 'Artifact' });
157:     const input = [owned(solRing, 4)];
158:     applySingletonLimits(input);
159:     assert.strictEqual(input[0]!.quantity, 4);
160:   });
161: });
